chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) who said:
Verily, the Divine Proof cannot be established for Allah against His creatures except by an Imam, until He is recognised.

key_terms.الإمام: Imam — the divinely appointed leader and guide, the living proof of God on earth
key_terms.الحجة: hujjah — the Proof or Authority of God, the binding argument that establishes human accountability before God
key_terms.يُعرَف: to be recognised/known — the active recognition of the Imam, implying wilaya (guardianship) and adherence

ai.seo_question: Why is an Imam necessary for God's proof to be established over creation according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) declares a foundational principle of Shia theology: that God's proof (hujjah) against humanity cannot be complete without a living Imam to guide and be recognized. This teaching, transmitted through a chain of trustworthy narrators, establishes the necessity of Imamate as the means by which God's authority is made manifest and accountability becomes possible. The original audience — students of early Shia learning — would understand 'hujjah' as the legal and theological concept of God's binding argument against His creation, making humanity responsible for their beliefs and actions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya Al Attar, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Dawood Al Raqyy, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Abd Al-Salih<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘The Divine Authority of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> cannot be established upon His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures except by an Imam<sup>asws</sup> until He<sup>azwj</sup> is recognised’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya al-‘Attar has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn abu ‘Amayr from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Dawud al-Riqqi from the pious man (a.s.)
the following “Allah’s holding people accountable remains unjustified without the Imam who would teach people about Him.”
